quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a residential district if no other limit is posted?
questions.explanation: The normal speed limit in a residential district is 25 miles per hour. If a different speed limit is posted, follow that sign instead.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people or vehicles cannot be seen from 500 feet away.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, you must let drivers who arrived before you go first. Wait your turn before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What is the correct rule at a four-way stop?

options.text: Drivers may demand the right-of-way, even if it causes an accident.
The driver who arrives first should go first.
Drivers may slow down and go if the road looks clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first should go first.
questions.explanation: The driver who arrives first at a four-way stop should go first. Drivers go through in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the same speed to get better traction.
Press the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When water on the road makes your tires lose grip, this is called hydroplaning. Slow down gradually and do not use your brakes if this happens.

questions.question: Can you use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night?
questions.explanation: You cannot use only parking lights to drive at night. You must use your headlights when visibility is low.

questions.question: When must you use your headlights?
questions.explanation: You must turn on your headlights between sunset and sunrise. Also use them any time visibility is reduced.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in foggy weather?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
It is okay to drive at the speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams reflect back and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Using a handheld device to read, type, or send messages while driving is:

options.text: A secondary offense with a fine of $50 to $100.
A secondary offense with a fine of $200 to $500.
Not a traffic violation in Nebraska.

questions.correctAnswerText: A secondary offense with a fine of $200 to $500.
questions.explanation: Using a handheld device to read, type, or send messages while driving is a secondary offense. The fine is between $200 and $500.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When you stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on. This makes sure other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop. Stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Is it against the law to drive at night using only parking lights?
questions.explanation: Yes, it is against the law. You must use your headlights when driving at night.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they may not see you. If you think another car is about to hit you, sound your horn right away.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is on top and green is on the bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear orange or yellow vests or bright jackets. They use paddles and flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers may not see you directly behind them. Keep extra distance from these vehicles. Also, large vehicles block your view of the road ahead, so increase your following distance to see around them.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need extra effort to steer. Slow down and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because other cars are unlikely to be coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Never pass across a solid yellow line.

questions.question: You see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Start a left turn from the far left lane of a one-way street.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for another train on any track. Do not move until all gates are raised and all warning signals have stopped flashing.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: The amount of food in your stomach.

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws. They are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green text or symbols.

questions.question: When a traffic light is red but shows a green arrow, when can you proceed?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: You may proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane and the road ahead is clear. This applies whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.
